text:
The best bank account for a UK sole trader or small business depends heavily on how you handle payments, whether you need built-in accounting software for Making Tax Digital (MTD), and if you deposit physical cash.

For most digital-first businesses, Starling Bank and Mettle (by NatWest) are the strongest all-round choices because they charge zero monthly fees and include free UK bank transfers.   
AccountingStack

Top UK Business Bank Accounts Compared
Provider	Best For	Monthly Fee	UK Transfers	Cash Deposits	FSCS Protected?
Starling Bank	Best overall (Sole Traders & Ltds)	£0	Free	0.7% (£3 min) via Post Office	Yes (up to £120k)
Mettle (by NatWest)	Best for free accounting software	£0	Free	£2.75 flat fee at Post Office	No (e-money safeguarded)
Monzo Business	Best for tax pots & budgeting	£0 (Lite) / £9 (Pro)	Free	£1 flat fee (PayPoint / Post Office)	Yes (up to £120k)
Tide	Fast sign-up & extra admin tools	£0 (Lite) / £12.49+	5 free/mo, then 20p	Varies (PayPoint / Post Office)	Mixed (ClearBank is protected; e-money isn't)
Virgin Money M Account	High street backing with no fee	£0	Free	Branch / Post Office fees apply	Yes (up to £120k)
Wise Business	International clients & multi-currency	£0 (£50 one-off setup for full details)	Low/free domestic	Not supported	No (e-money safeguarded)
Which One Should You Pick?

Pick Starling Bank if you want the best all-rounder: You get full UK banking protection (FSCS up to £120,000), free domestic transfers, separate "Spaces" to set aside tax money, and free feeds into Xero, QuickBooks, and FreeAgent. If you already hold a personal Starling account, you can manage both in the same app.   
BusinessComparison

Pick Mettle if you want to save on accounting software: Backed by NatWest, Mettle includes FreeAgent (usually ~£19/month) completely free as long as you make at least one transaction a month. This is especially valuable for Making Tax Digital (MTD) quarterly submissions. (Note: Mettle operates under an e-money licence rather than a full banking licence, so funds are safeguarded rather than FSCS-protected.)   
AccountingStack
+ 2

Pick Monzo Business Pro (£9/month) if you want automated tax admin: While the free Lite tier covers basic banking, upgrading to Pro unlocks automatic Tax Pots (which automatically sweep a percentage of incoming payments into a separate pot for HMRC), integrated invoicing, and live accounting software syncs.   
BusinessComparison

Pick Virgin Money M Account or NatWest if you want a traditional bank: Virgin Money offers permanent fee-free digital banking with 0.25% cashback on debit card spend and branch access. NatWest offers up to 24 months of free banking for startups/switchers plus free FreeAgent, though standard monthly and transaction fees kick in after the introductory period.   
Forbes
+ 1

Pick Wise Business if you invoice in USD, EUR, or other currencies: High street and UK digital banks typically charge 1%–3% on foreign exchange. Wise gives you local bank details in multiple currencies and converts money at the mid-market exchange rate for a tiny transparent fee.   
BusinessComparison

Two Quick Tips Before You Apply

Sole trader vs. Limited Company: If you are a sole trader, you aren't legally required to have a business account, though most personal banks prohibit using a personal account for business in their T&Cs. If you are a Limited Company, you must open a separate business account in the company's name.

Watch out for FSCS limits: If you are a sole trader and hold both your personal and business accounts with the same bank (e.g., Starling or Monzo), the £120,000 FSCS protection limit applies to your combined balances across both accounts.   
BusinessComparison

To help narrow this down, are you trading as a sole trader or a Limited Company, and do you expect to deposit much physical cash or handle foreign currencies?
